insimulo.definition: īn-simulō āvī, ātus, āre, to make suspected, charge, accuse, blame, impeach: tu me insimulas, bring a charge against: Criminibus virum, O.: vilicus cum impulso tuo insimulatus esset: insimulatus falso crimine senatus,…

insincerus.definition: īn-sincērus adj., spoiled, corrupted: cruor, V.

insinuatio.definition: īnsinuātiō ōnis, f insinuo.—In rhet., a conciliation of favor, insinuating style.

insinuo.definition: īn-sinuō āvī, ātus, āre, to thrust in, push in, make a way: potestas in forum insinuandi: quācumque data intervalla essent, insinuabant ordines suos, pushed forward their files, L.—With pron reflex., to find a way in,…

insipiens.definition: īnsipiēns entis, adj. with comp. 2 in + sapiens, unwise, foolish: fortunatus: ego insipientior quam illi ipsi.

insipientia.definition: īnsipientia ae, f insipiens, unwisdom, folly: animi.

insisto.definition: īn-sistō stitī, —, ere, to set foot, take a stand, stand on, step on, tread on: firmiter, hold their ground, Cs.: ut proximi iacentibus insisterent, stepped upon, Cs.: vestigiis abeuntium, L.: huic (saxo) institerat f…

insitio.definition: īnsitiō ōnis, f 1 in+1 SA-, an ingrafting, grafting: delectant insitiones.—The time of grafting, O.

insitivus.definition: īnsitīvus adj. insitus, ingrafted, grafted: pira, H.—Fig.: Gracchus, pretended: disciplinae, imported: liberi, spurious, Ph.

insitor.definition: insitor ōris, m 1 SA-, an ingrafter, Pr.

insociabilis.definition: īn-sociābilis e, adj., without social ties, not to be bound in friendship, unsociable: gens, L.: homines omni generi humano, L.

insolabiliter.definition: īnsōlābiliter adv. solor, inconsolably: dolens, H.

insolens.definition: īn-solēns ntis, adj., unaccustomed, unusual, not used, contrary to custom: Quid tu Athenas insolens? T.: aspera aequora Emirabitur insolens, H.: in dicendo, inexperienced: infamiae: belli, Cs. —Excessive, immoderate, …

insolentia.definition: īnsolentia ae, f insolens, unusualness, strangeness, novelty: fori iudiciorumque: itineris, S.: voluptatum.—Of language, novelty, strangeness, affectedness: orationis: verborum.—Want of moderation, haughtiness, arroga…

insolesco.definition: īn-solēscō —, —, ere, inch, to grow haughty, become elated: per licentiam animus insolescit, S.: rebus secundis, Ta.

insolidus.definition: īn-solidus adj., not solid, tender: herba, O.

insolitus.definition: īn-solitus adj., unaccustomed, unused, unfamiliar, strange: feminae in virorum conventum: insolitae fugiunt in flumina phocae, i. e. contrary to their custom, V.: ad laborem, Cs.: rerum bellicarum, S.: eius tumultūs e…

insomnia.definition: īnsomnia ae, f insomnis, sleeplessness, want of sleep, watching: te adiget horsum insomnia, T.: insomniis fatigari, S.: insomniis carere.

insomnis.definition: īnsomnis e, adj. 2 in + somnus, sleepless, wakeful: ille noctes insomnis agit, H.: draco, O.: nox, V.

insono.definition: īn-sonō uī, —, āre, to resound: Boreae cum spiritus Insonat Aegaeo, roars over, V.: caeli delapsa per auras Insonuit, resounded, V.: pennis, rustle with, O.: calamis, make music with, O.: insonuitque flagello, cracked…

insons.definition: īn-sōns ntis, adj., guiltless, innocent: amicus, V.: publici consili, L.: si regni crimine insons fuerit, L.—As subst m.: insontes sicuti sontes circumvenire, S.—Harmless: Cerberus, H.: casa, O.

insopitus.definition: īn-sōpītus adj., sleepless, wakeful: draco, O.

inspecto.definition: (īnspectō —, —, āre), freq. inspicio, to look at, observe, view.—Only P. praes.: ipsis inspectantibus, before their very eyes: inspectante exercitu: inspectante ipso, Cs.

insperatus.definition: īn-spērātus adj., unhoped for, unlooked for, unexpected, unforeseen: gaudium, T.: praesidium: tellus, V.: pluma, unwelcome, H.: omnibus consilium: nihil tam insperatum accidere potuit, L.— As subst n.: ex insperato, u…

inspicio.definition: īnspiciō spēxī, spectus, ere 1 in+specio, to look into, look upon, inspect, consider, contemplate, examine, survey: in vitas omnium, T.: cupiditas inspiciendi: cum Romam inspexerit Eos, O.: urbīs, H.: ranarum viscera,…

inspico.definition: īnspīcō —, —, ere spica, to cut in the form of an ear of corn, sharpen: ferro faces, V.

inspiro.definition: īn-spīrō āvī, ātus, āre, to blow upon, breathe into, inspire: conchae, O.: Se (Fames) viro inspirat, O.—Fig., to inspire, excite, inflame: occultum ignem, V: animas, O.—To instil, implant: venenum Morsibus, V.: virus,…

inspoliatus.definition: īn-spoliātus adj., not plundered, not made spoil: arma, V.

instabilis.definition: īn-stabilis e, adj., not steadfast, unsteady, unstable, tottering, not firm: ingressus, L.: cymbae, V.: naves, Cu.: acies, shaken, L.—Giving no support: tellus, O.—Fig., unstable, inconstant, changeable, fickle: insta…

instanter.definition: (īnstanter) adv., earnestly, pressingly.—Only comp: instantius concurrere, Ta.

instantia.definition: īnstantia ae, f insto, an impendence, approach: futura quorum vera erit instantia.

instar.definition: īnstar n indecl, an image, likeness, resemblance, appearance: terra quasi puncti instar obtinet, looks almost like: parvum instar eorum, quae concepisset, a small specimen, L.: omnia vix minimi momenti instar habent, …

instauratio.definition: īnstaurātiō ōnis, f instauro, a renewing, repetition: ludorum: ludi ex instauratione paran tur, L.

instaurativus.definition: īnstaurātīvus adj. instauro, instituted anew, begun afresh: ludi.

instauro.definition: īnstaurō āvī, ātus, āre, to establish, ordain: choros, V.—To renew, repeat, resume: instaurandae caedis potestas: novum de integro bellum, L.: infestis pugnam sagittis, Iu.: diem donis, celebrates with repeated offeri…

insterno.definition: īn-sternō strāvī, strātus, ere, to cover, cover over, spread upon: insternor pelle leonis, V.: pontīs altos, floored (i. e. constructed), V.: pulpita tignis, laid the stage over a scaffolding, H.

instigator.definition: īnstīgātor ōris, m instigo, a stimulator, instigator: sibi quisque, Ta.

instigatrix.definition: īnstīgātrīx īcis, f instigo, she that instigates: adversum alqm, Ta.

instigo.definition: īnstīgō āvī, ātus, āre STIG-, to goad on, urge, stimulate, stir, set on, incite, instigate: si hic non insanit satis suā sponte, instiga, T.: instigante te, at your instigation: sequentem studiis, V.: Romanos in Hanni…

instillo.definition: īn-stīllō āvī, ātus, āre, to pour in by drops, drop in, instil: lumini oleum: (oleum) caulibus, H.—To drop upon, fall on: guttae saxa instillant. —Fig., to instil, infuse: tuae litterae mihi quiddam quasi animulae ins…

instimulator.definition: īnstimulātor ōris, m instimulo, a stimulator: seditionis.

instimulo.definition: īn-stimulō —, —, āre, to goad, urge on, stimulate: Bacchas sonis, O.: Venerem verbis, O.

instinctor.definition: īnstinctor ōris, m STIG-, an instigator: sceleris, Ta.

instinguo.definition: (īn-stinguō) —, stinctus, ere, to instigate, incite, impel (only P. pass.): furore et audaciā, impelled: vocibus, animated, L.: furiis, inspired, L.

instita.definition: īnstita ae, f a border, flounce of a lady's tunic: Quarum subsutā talos tegit instita veste, H.: longa, O.: nulla, i. e. no lady, O.

institor.definition: īnstitor ōris, m STA-, a factor, broker, huckster, hawker, peddler: chirographorum: amata multum institoribus, H.: ipse mercis, peddler of his own wares, L.: hibernae tegetis, Iu.

instituo.definition: īnstituō uī, ūtus, ere 1 in+statuo, to put in place, plant, fix, set: vestigia nuda sinistri pedis, V.: hominem in animum, i. e. to set one's heart on, T.—Of troops, to draw up, arrange: duplici acie institutā , Cs.: …

institutio.definition: īnstitūtiō ōnis, f instituo, disposition, arrangement: rerum: institutionem suam conservare, custom.—Instruction, education: doctoris: de aliquā re: Graecis institutionibus eruditi, learning.

insto.definition: īn-stō stitī, statūrus, āre, to stand upon, take a position: iugis, V.—To draw nigh, approach, be at hand, impend: partus instabat prope, T.: nox instabat, S.: ea quae videntur instare: instant ludi: cum illi iter ins…

instrenuus.definition: īn-strēnuus adj., sluggish, spiritless: animus, T.

instrepo.definition: īn-strepō uī, itus, ere, to resound, rattle, creak: sub pondere faginus axis Instrepat, V.

instringo.definition: (īn-stringō) —, ictus, ere, to bind, fasten.— — Only P. pass.: Instricta fides gemmis, inlaid, O.

instructio.definition: īnstrūctiō ōnis, f STRV-, an array: instructione aspectuque signorum pulsus.

instructor.definition: īnstrūctor ōris, m instruo, a preparer: convivi.

instrumentum.definition: īnstrūmentum ī, n STRV-, an implement, utensil, tool, instrument: tela et cetera instrumenta militiae, S.: crudelia instrumenta necis, O.—Collect. in sing, instruments, apparatus, material, stock, furniture: instrumen…

instruo.definition: īn-struō ūxī, ūctus, ere, to build in, insert: Eam (contabulationem) in parietes, Cs.—Of troops, to form, set in order, draw up, array: ad instruendum spatium, L.: hosce, T.: exercitum, S.: aciem: aciem instructum hab…

insuavis.definition: īn-suāvis e, adj. with comp. and sup, unpleasant, disagreeable: vita: haberi, H.: insuavissima littera.

insudo.definition: īn-sūdō —, —, āre, to sweat on, stain with sweat: quīs (libellis) manus insudet volgi, H.

insuefactus.definition: īnsuēfactus adj. insuesco + facio, accustomed, habituated (adsuetus): equi, Cs.

insuesco.definition: īn-suēscō suēvī (-suērat, Ta.), suē tus, ere, to habituate oneself, become accustomed, be inured: mentiri, T.: amare, S.: militem victoriā frui, L.— To accustom, habituate: hoc me Ut fugerem, H.: ita se a pueris insue…

insuetus.definition: īn-suētus adj. P. of insuesco, unaccustomed, unused, inexperienced: contumeliae: huius generis pugnae, Cs.: navigandi, Cs.: male audiendi, N.: vera audire, L.: acies inferre pedestrīs, V.: miratur nemus insuetum Scuta…

insula.definition: īnsula ae, f 1 SAL-, an island, isle: Delos: Rheni amnis, Ta.— A part of Rome encircled by the Tiber, O.—A part of Syracuse cut off by an arm of the sea, L., C.—An enclosed court, tenement for poor families: Clodi.

insulanus.definition: īnsulānus ī, m insula, an islander.

insulsitas.definition: īnsulsitās ātis, f insulsus, tastelessness, insipidity, silliness, want of wit: eorum: harum rerum: orationis.

insulsus.definition: īnsulsus adj. with sup. 2 in+salsus, unsalted, without taste, coarse: gula.—Fig., bungling, awkward: bipennis, Iu.—Tasteless, insipid, silly, absurd: Fatuos est, insulsus, T.: in verbo non insulsum genus (ridiculi): a…

insulto.definition: īnsultō āvī, ātus, āre, freq. insilio, to spring at, leap upon, leap, bound, jump, spring: fremit aequore toto Insultans sonipes, V.: busto, H.: Fluctibus insultavere carinae, O.: istas (forīs) calcibus, T.: nemora av…

insum.definition: īn-sum īnfuī, inesse, to be in, be upon: ibi inerat pictura (i. e. in conclavi), T.: Hic . . . minotaurus inest, V.: in urbe: quae (fercula) inerant canistris, H.: inerant lunaria fronti Cornua, O.— Fig., to be contai…

insumo.definition: īn-sūmō sūmpsī, sūmptus, ere, to take for, apply, expend: ut nullus teruncius insumatur in quemquam: non est melius quo insumere possis, H.: Nullum ultra verbum, quin amares, etc., waste no word, to hinder, etc., H.—F…

insuo.definition: īn-suō uī, ūtus, ere, to sew in, sew into, sew up: insutus in culeum: terga boum plumbo insuto, i. e. the cestus, V.: patrio (infans) Insuitur femori, O.: insutum vestibus aurum, embroidered, O.

insuper.definition: īn-super adv., above, on the top, overhead: insuper bipedalibus trabibus immissis, Cs.: montīs insuper altos Imposuit, V.: cumulatis in aquas sarcinis, insuper incumbebant, L.: circumvelari, O.—From above: iugum insup…

insuperabilis.definition: īn-superābilis e, adj., that cannot be passed over, insurmountable: Alpium transitus, L.—Invincible: genus bello, V.—Inevitable: fatum, O.

insurgo.definition: īn-surgō surrēxī, surrēctus, ere, to rise up, rise, lift oneself: attolli et insurgere, Ta.: (serpens) arduus insurgens, V.: Altior insurgens heros, V.: Ostendit dextram insurgens Entellus (for the blow), V.: insurgit…

insusurro.definition: īn-susurrō āvī, ātus, āre, to whisper to, insinuate, suggest: alteri: ad aurem familiariter: in aurem: mihi cantilenam: navigandi nobis tempus esse.

intabesco.definition: in-tābēscō buī, —, ere, inch, to waste away, pine away: cum semel fixae cibo Intabuissent pupulae, H.: videndo, to pine with envy, O.—To melt away, dissolve: ut intabescere Igne cerae solent, O.

intactus.definition: in-tāctus adj. with comp, untouched, uninjured, intact: cervix iuvencae, not broken to the yoke, V.: boves, H.: nix, L.: exercitus, L.: intactis adsidere muris, L.: nemo intactus profugit, S.: Britannus, unsubdued, H.…

intaminatus.definition: intāminātus adj. TAG-, unsullied, undefiled: honores, H.

integellus.definition: 'integellus adj. dim. integer, pretty safe, in fair condition: alqm praestare: alqd, Ct.'

integer.definition: integer tegra, tegrum, adj. with comp. integrior and sup. integerrimus 2 in-+TAG-, untouched, unhurt, entire, whole, complete: annus: integro die, i. e. with the day before us, H.: quarum (sublicarum) pars inferior in…

intego.definition: in-tegō tēxī, tēctus, ere, to cover over: reliqua pars scrobis virgultis integebatur, Cs.: cum primā luce densa nebula saltum intexit, L.—To protect: vidit vallo etiam integi Romanos, L.

integrasco.definition: integrāscō —, —, ere, inch. integro, to begin anew, break out afresh: hoc malum integrascit, T.

integratio.definition: integrātiō ōnis, f integro, a renewing, restoring: Amantium irae amoris integratio, T.

integritas.definition: integritās ātis, f integer, completeness, soundness: corporis: valetudinis.—Fig., purity, correctness: Latini sermonis.—Blamelessness, innocence, integrity: vitae, S.: integritas atque innocentia: vitae, N.: mulierem …

integro.definition: integrō āvī, ātus, āre integer, to make whole: artūs in pravum elapsos, i. e. set, Ta.—To renew, begin again: lacrimas, L.: carmen, V.—Fig., to recreate, refresh: animus admiratione integratur.

integumentum.definition: integumentum ī, n intego, a covering: lanx cum integumentis, lids, L.—That which conceals, a covering: frontis: flagitiorum: nequitia frontis involuta integumentis.

intellegentia.definition: intellegentia (intellig-) ae, f intellegens, discernment, understanding, intelligence: pars animi, intellegentiae particeps: in quibus (gustu et odoratu) est intellegentia.—Understanding, knowledge: iuris: Eam calamit…

intellego.definition: intellegō (not intelligō), ēxī (intellēxtī , T., C.; intellēgit, S.), ēctus inter+lego, to come to know, see into, perceive, understand, discern, comprehend, gather: quod ubi intellexi: id quod omnes intellegunt: cum …

intemperanter.definition: 'intemperanter adv. with comp. intemperans, immoderately, extravagantly, intemperately: abuti otio: intemperantius opibus suis uti: aviditate caedis intemperantius secuti, too rashly, Cs.'

intemperantia.definition: intemperantia ae, f intemperans, want of moderation, excess, extravagance, intemperance: menti inimica: vini, immoderate use, L.—Arrogance, insolence, insubordination: Pausaniae, N.: suā intemperantiā, nimiāque licent…

intemperies.definition: (in-temperiēs) — (only acc. and abl.), f want of moderation, irregularity, excess, inclemency: caeli, L.: aquarum, immoderate rains, L.— Fig., of conduct, excess, outrage, fury: amici: unius: cohortium, Ta.

intempestivus.definition: in-tempestīvus adj., untimely, unseasonable, inopportune: amicitia numquam est: Minerva, i. e. unseasonable spinning, O.: honos, Ta.

intempestus.definition: intempestus adj. 2 in+tempus, unseasonable, unpropitious, dark: nox, the dead of night.— Person.: intempesta silet Nox, dismal Night (mother of the Furies), V.—Unwholesome, unhealthy: Graviscae, V.

intendo.definition: in-tendō dī, tus, ere, to stretch out, reach forth, extend: dextram ad statuam: manūs, O.: iubet intendi bracchia velis, V.—To stretch, spread out, lay, fasten, extend: intendentibus tenebris, spreading, L.: tabernacu…

intentio.definition: intentiō ōnis, f 2 TA-, a stretching, straining, tension: corporis.— Fig., an exertion, effort, application, attention: animi: lusūs, to play, L.— A purpose, intention: adversariorum.

intento.definition: intentō āvī, ātus, āre, intens. intendo, to aim, direct, wield in hostility, stretch threateningly: dolor ardentīs faces intentat: pauci Romanum imperium intentantes, i. e. holding up as a threat, L.: haec sica intent…

intepeo.definition: in-tepeō —, —, ēre, to be lukewarm: lacus, Pr.

intepesco.definition: īn-tepēscō puī, —, ere, inch, to become lukewarm, be warmed: strata membris tuis, O.— Poet.: Ut semel intepuit mucro, felt blood, V.

inter.definition: inter praep. with acc. ANA-, between, betwixt: (mons) inter Sequanos et Helvetios, Cs.: inter me et Brundisium esse.—With more than two objects, among, amid, in the midst of, surrounded by: inter hostium tela versari:…

interamenta.definition: interāmenta ōrum, n inter, the interior woodwork (of a ship of war): navium, L.

interaresco.definition: inter-ārēscō —, —, ere, inch, to become dry, dry up, decay: nihil interarescere debet.

intercalaris.definition: intercalāris e, adj. intercalo, of insertion, to be inserted, intercalary: Kalendae, of an intercalary month: Kalendae priores, of the first intercalary month (Caesar introduced two).

intercalarius.definition: intercalārius adj. intercalaris, for insertion, intercalary: mensis, L.: Kalendae, of an intercalary month, L.—As subst. (sc. mensis).

intercalo.definition: inter-calō āvī, ātus, āre, to proclaim an insertion in the calendar, insert, intercalate (a prerogative of the pontifices): ut pugnes, ne intercaletur. —To put off, postpone: intercalata poena, L.

intercapedo.definition: intercapēdō īnis, f intercapio, an interruption, interval, respite: scribendi.

intercedo.definition: inter-cēdō cessī, cessus, ere, to come between, intervene, be between: palus, quae intercedebat, Cs.: inter singulas legiones impedimentorum numerum intercedere, Cs.—To occur, happen, come to pass: neque ullam rem int…

interceptio.definition: interceptiō ōnis, f CAP-, a taking away: poculi.

interceptor.definition: interceptor ōris, m CAP-, an intercepter, usurper, embezzler: praedae, L.: donativi, Ta.

intercessio.definition: intercessiō ōnis, f 1 CAD-, a mediation, suretyship: mea intercessio parata est.—An intervention, interposition, protest, veto: tribunicia, Cs.: empta: remittere intercessionem, L.

intercessor.definition: intercessor ōris, m 1 CAD-, one who interposes, a mediator, surety: intercessorem quaerere: isto intercessore legati non adierunt, through his interference: rei malae.—An interferer, protester, adversary, preventer: s…

intercino.definition: intercinō —, —, ere inter+cano, to sing between: neu quid medios intercinat actūs, H.

intercipio.definition: intercipiō cēpī, ceptus, ere inter+capio, to seize in passing, intercept: quod nos capere oportet, T.: pila intercepta remittere, Cs.: venenum, take the poison intended for another: numerum iumentorum, Cs.: ab suis in…

intercludo.definition: interclūdō ūsī, ūsus, ere inter+claudo, to shut out, shut off, cut off, hinder, stop, block up, intercept: virtus voluptatis aditū s intercludat necesse est: interclusis itineribus, Cs.: illos ponti Interclusit hiemps…

interclusio.definition: interclūsiō ōnis, f intercludo, a stopping, entire suspension: animae (in speaking).

intercolumnium.definition: intercolumnium ī, n inter+columna, a space between two columns, intercolumniation.

intercurro.definition: inter-currō currī, cursus, ere, to run between, intervene, mediate: qui intercurrerent, misimus trīs principes civitatis.—Of time, to hasten meanwhile: ipse interim Veios intercurrit, L.—Fig., t<*> mingle, be associat…

intercurso.definition: inter-cursō —, —, āre, freq. intercurro, to run in, intervene: intercursantibus barbaris, L.

intercursus.definition: (intercursus ūs), m 1 CEL-.—Only abl. sing, a running between, intervention, interposition: periculum intercursu filii propulsatum, L.: consulum intercursu rixa sedata est, L.

interdico.definition: inter-dīcō dīxī, dictus, ere, to interpose by speaking, forbid, prohibit, interdict: praetor interdixit: non tulit ut interdicatur: quae interdicta sunt: interdicta voluptas, H.: Cassivellauno ne noceat, Cs.: praecipi…

interdictio.definition: interdictiō ōnis, f DIC-, a prohibiting, forbidding: aquae et ignis, banishment: finium, L.

interdictum.definition: interdictum ī, n P. of interdico, a forbiden thing: si interdicta petes, H.—A prohibition: deorum.—Of the praetor, a provisional decree, interlocutory order, prohibition, interdict: praetorum interdicta tollentur: tyr…

interdiu.definition: interdiū adv. DIV-, during the day, in the daytime, by day: nec nocte nec interdiu, L.

interductus.definition: (interductus ūs), m DVC-, interpunctuation; only abl.

interdum.definition: inter-dum adv., sometimes, occasionally, now and then: Pecuniam neglegere est interdum lucrum, T.: saepe gratiā interdum iurgiis trahendo tempus, S.: lacrimas tenere, Cs.: dicere: interdum . . . interdum, now . . . no…

interea.definition: inter-eā adv., meanwhile, in the meantime, in the interim: saepe interea mihi senex Narrabat, T.: dies advenit: quietus erat, S.: interea loci, in the meantime, T.—Meanwhile, nevertheless, however: tu interea non cess…

intereo.definition: inter-eō iī, itūrus, īre (perf. interīsse, C.), to go among, be lost: ut interit magnitudine maris stilla muriae.—Fig., to perish, go to ruin, decay, die: pauci interiere, S.: statuae intereunt tempestate: tormentorum…

interequito.definition: inter-equitō —, —, āre, to ride between: ipse interequitans, L.: ordines, L.: agmina, Cu.

interfatio.definition: interfātiō ōnis, f interfor, a speaking between, interruption.

interfector.definition: interfector ōris, m inter+2 FAC-, a slayer, murderer, assassin: eorum, C., L.

interfectrix.definition: interfectrīx īcis, f interfector, a murderess: nepotis, Ta.

interfluo.definition: inter-fluō —, —, ere, to flow between: quantum interfluit fretum, L.: media moenia, Cu.: Romanos Cheruscosque, Ta.

interfor.definition: inter-for ātus, ārī, dep., to interrupt in speaking: Venus sic interfata est, V.: priusquam postulatum perageret Appius interfatur, L.: Phaeneas interfatus, interrupting, L.

interim.definition: interim adv. inter+old acc. from 2 I-, meanwhile, in the meantime: interim Romā subito profectus est: interim cotidie Caesar Aeduos frumentum flagitare, Cs.: interim dum, etc., T.: et tamen interim, S.—However, nevert…

interimo.definition: interimō or interemō ēmī, ēmptus, or ēmtus inter+emo, to take from the midst, take away, do away with, abolish: interimendorum sacrorum causā.—To destroy, slay, kill: interemptam oportuit, T.: plures eo proelio intere…

interior.definition: interior ius, gen. ōris inter, inner, interior, middle: aedium pars: spatium, O.: In interiore parte ut maneam, i. e. in the women's apartment, T.: domus, inner part, V.: epistula, body: motu cietur interiore et suo: …

interitio.definition: interitiō ōnis, f inter+I-, destruction, ruin: aratorum.

interlabor.definition: inter-lābor —, ī, dep., to flow between.—In tmesis: inter enim labentur aquae, percolate, V.

interlino.definition: inter-linō lēvī, litus, ere, to smear between, spread between, join with: caementa luto, L.: murus bitumine interlitus, Cu.—To make erasures in, alter by erasing: testamentum.

interloquor.definition: inter-loquor locūtus, ī, dep., to interrupt in speaking: mihi, T.

interluceo.definition: inter-lūceō lūxī, —, ēre, to shine in the midst: quaedam animalia interlucent (in amber), Ta.—To lighten at intervals, shine irregularly.—Impers.: noctu interluxisse, L.—Fig., to be manifest, be plainly visible: ordin…

interlunium.definition: interlūnium ī, n interlunis, the time of new moon.—Plur., H.

interluo.definition: inter-luō —, —, ere.—Of streams, to wash under, flow between: pontus arva et urbīs interluit, V.: quosque secans interluit Allia, V.: saxa interluens unda, Cu.

intermisceo.definition: inter-misceō miscuī, mīxtus, ēre, to mix among, intermix, mingle: turbabant equos pedites intermixti, L.: tibi undam, V.: patriis petita Verba foris, H.: intermixti hostibus cognoscunt, L.

intermissio.definition: intermissiō ōnis, f intermitto, a breaking off, intermission, interruption, discontinuance: forensis operae: sine ullā intermissione: per intermissiones has, L.: epistularum, of correspondence: verborum, i. e. abruptn…

intermitto.definition: inter-mittō mīsī, missus, ere, to leave off, intermit, omit, suspend, interrupt, neglect: iter, proelium, Cs.: hoc intermisi, quoad non licuit: laborem, O.: Intermissa diu bella, H.: litteras mittere: non intermittit …

intermorior.definition: inter-morior mortuus, ī, dep., to die off, die out: intermoriuntur reliquiae coniurationis: ignis, Cu.: intermori civitatem sinere, L.: officium apud me intermoriturum, i. e. to be forgotten.

intermundia.definition: intermundia ōrum, n plur. inter+mundus, spaces between worlds.

intermuralis.definition: inter-mūrālis e, adj., between the walls: amnis, i. e. ditch, L.

internascor.definition: (inter-nāscor) nātus, ī, dep., to grow between, spring up in the way: internata virgulta, L.: internatae saxis herbae, Ta.

internecio.definition: interneciō (-niciō) ōnis, f inter+1 NEC-, a massacre, slaughter, carnage, extermination, destruction: internicione civĩs liberare: bella ad internecionem gesta, N.: ad internecionem caesi, all put to the sword, L.: ad…

internecto.definition: inter-nectō —, —, ere, to bind together, bind up: ut fibula crinem Auro internectat, V.

interniteo.definition: inter-niteō —, —, ēre, to shine through, shine at intervals: si qua sidera internitebant, Cu.

internodium.definition: inter-nōdium ī, n inter+nodus, the space between two joints: quā facit internodia poples, O.

internosco.definition: inter-nōscō nōvī, nōtus, ere, to know apart, distinguish, discern: fures: blandus amicus a vero internosci potest: mendacem verumque amicum, H.: visa vera sint, anne falsa.

internuntia.definition: inter-nūntia ae, f a mediator, messenger: aves internuntiae Iovis: Iudaea: caeli, Iu.

internuntio.definition: inter-nūntiō —, —, ēre, to exchange messages, negotiate: utri transgrederentur, L.

internuntius.definition: inter-nūntius ī, a mediator, messenger, gobetween: Nequis internuntius ad istam curset, T.: internuntiis ultro citroque missis, Cs.: totius rei, L.: Iovis interpretes internuntiique, i. e. the augurs.

internus.definition: internus adj. inter, inward, internal: arae, O.—Fig.: mala, domestic, S.: discordiae, Ta.

intero.definition: in-terō trīvī, trītus, ere, to rub in, crumble in. — Prov.: Tute hoc intrīsti, tibi omnest exedendum, you have your own mess to swallow, T.

interpellatio.definition: interpellatiō ōnis, f interpello, a speaking between, interruption.

interpellator.definition: interpellātor ōris, m interpello, an interrupter, disturber: se oblectare sine interpellatoribus.

interpello.definition: interpellō āvī, ātus, āre 1 PAL-, to interrupt, break in upon: interpellando trahere tempus, S.: Interpellandi locus erat, H.: alqm ingressum in sermonem, Cs.: nihil te interpellabo: ab alqo interpellari, Cu.—To urge …

interpolo.definition: interpolō āvī, ātus, āre interpolus (old), furbished, to polish, furbish, dress up: togam praetextam, dye anew.—Of writings, to interpolate, alter, falsify: aliquid.

interpono.definition: inter-pōnō posuī, posītus, ere, to put between, place among, interpose, insert, intersperse: ubi spatium . . . pilae interponuntur, Cs.: ne interpositi quidem elephanti militem deterrebant, L.: lateri vinculum lapides…

interpositio.definition: interpositiō ōnis, f interpositus, an insertion, introduction: personarum: una (of words).

interpres.definition: interpres etis, m and f PRAT-, a middleman, mediator, broker, factor, negotiator: interpretes corrumpendi iudici: pacis, L.: divūm, messenger (i. e. Mercury), V.: harum curarum Iuno, i. e. of the anxieties of love, V.…

interpretatio.definition: interpretātiō ōnis, f interpretor, an explanation, exposition, interpretation: egere interpretatione: facilis, L.: foederis, meaning: sinistra erga eminentīs, Ta.

interpretor.definition: interpretor ātus, ārī, dep. interpres, to explain, expound, interpret, understand, conclude, infer, comprehend: si interpretari velis: religiones, Cs.: somnia: sententiam tuam: ad voluntatem, L.: ut plerique quaereren…

interpunctio.definition: interpunctiō ōnis, f interpunctus, a punctuation, division by points: interpunctiones verborum.

interquiesco.definition: inter-quiēscō quēvī, —, ere, to rest awhile, pause: paululum.

interregnum.definition: inter-rēgnum ī, n an interval between two reigns, interregnum: interregni ineundi ratio: id ab re interregnum appellatum, L.—In the republic, a vacancy in the consulate (between the death or departure of the consuls a…

interritus.definition: 'in-territus adj., undaunted, undismayed, unterrified: Bracchia interritus extulit, V.: classis, fearless, V.: mens leti, not afraid, O.: voltus, Cu.'

interrogatio.definition: interrogātiō ōnis, f interrogo, a questioning, interrogation, question: mea: stultissimae.— A judicial inquiry, examination, C.: tribuni, L.: testium, Ta.—In logic, a conclusion from questions, syllogism: genus interr…

interrogatiuncula.definition: interrogātiuncula ae, f dim. interrogatio, a short argument, syllogism: minutae.

interrogo.definition: inter-rogō āvī, ātus, āre, to ask, question, inquire, interrogate: recte, T.: interrogandi facultas: testem: illud, put this question, L.: nil plus, have no more to ask, Iu.: quendam quaedam geometrica: interrogans, s…

interrumpo.definition: inter-rumpō rūpī, ruptus, ere, to break apart, break off, interrupt, break to pieces, break up: pontem fluminis, destroy, Cs.: pontem ferro, igni, L.— To break through, divide, scatter: interrupta acies, L.: extremum …

intersaepio.definition: inter-saepiō saepsī, saeptus, ēre, to fence about, hedge in, stop up, enclose, secure: foramina intersaepta: operibus quaedam, L.— To shut off, cut off, obstruct: iter: vallo urbem ab arce, L.

interscindo.definition: inter-scindō scidī, scissus, ere, to tear asunder, break down, divide, interrupt: pontem: aggerem, Cs.—To cut off, separate, part: Chalcis arto interscinditur freto, L.

intersero.definition: inter-serō —, —, ere, to place between, interpose, add: oscula mediis verbis, O.—Fig.: causam, se esse, etc., allege as a pretext, N.

interspiratio.definition: interspīrātiō ōnis, f interspiro, a catching of breath, pause for breathing.—Sing. and plur.

intersum.definition: inter-sum fuī, futūrus, esse, to be between, lie between: quas (segetes) inter et castra unus collis intererat, Cs.: ut Tiberis inter eos et pons interesset: via interest perangusta, L.—To intervene, elapse: inter pri…

intertexo.definition: (inter-texō) —, textus, ere, to intertwine, interweave.— Only P. perf.: flores hederis intertexti, O.: chlamys auro intertexta, V.

intertrimentum.definition: intertrīmentum ī, n 1 TER-, loss by attrition, waste: in auro, L.—Fig., loss, damage: sine magno intertrimento, T.: nullum intertrimenti vestigium.

interturbo.definition: inter-turbō —, —, āre, to make disturbance, T.

intervallum.definition: inter-vāllum ī, n—Prop., the space between palisades, an intermediate space, interval, distance: pari intervallo, at an equal distance, Cs.: quo consuerat intervallo, at the usual distance, Cs.: videt magnis intervall…

intervenio.definition: inter-veniō vēnī, ventus, īre, to come between, come upon, come in, intervene, interrupt: dum sedemus, intervenit, T.: casu equites interveniunt, Cs.: ex occulto: quotiens lascivum intervenit illud, etc., is introduce…

interventor.definition: interventor ōris, m BA-, a visitor, intruder: vacuus ab interventoribus dies.

interverto.definition: inter-vertō (-vortō) iī, sus, ere, to turn aside, divert, intercept, embezzle, squander: receptum (consulatum): interversā aedilitate, i. e. passing over: interverso regali hoc dono.

interviso.definition: inter-vīsō —, —, ere, to look after, inspect secretly: ipse crebro interviso.—To visit at times: nos: manipulos, Ta.

intervolito.definition: intervolitō —, —, āre, freq. intervolo, to flutter around: imbrem (carnis) intervolitando rapuisse (of brids), L.

intestabilis.definition: in-testābilis e, adj. with comp, infamous, execrable, detestable, abominable: homo, S.: saevitiā, Ta.: intestabilior et saevior, Ta.

intestato.definition: intestātō adv. abl. of intestatus, without a will, intestate: mortuus.

intestinum.definition: intestīnum ī, n intestinus, a gut: loto terram ferit intestino, Iu.: medium, mesentery: imum, rectum, N.—Usu. plur, the intestines, entrails, bowels: laborare ex intestinis: intestina poetae, Iu.

intestinus.definition: intestīnus adj. intus, inward, internal, intestine: malum: bella, civil, S.: caedes, of kindred, L.—Fig., in the mind, subjective (opp. oblatus).

intexo.definition: in-texō texuī, textus, ere, to weave in, inweave, interweave, plait, join together, interlace, surround, envelop: scutis viminibus intextis, Cs.: abiete costas, V.: Vestibus intexto Phrygiis spectabilis auro, O.: pyra…

intibum.definition: intibum ī, n endive, succory.—Plur., V., O.

intimus.definition: intimus or intumus adj. sup. ANA-, inmost, innermost, deepest, profound: in eo sacrario intimo: abdidit se in intimam Macedoniam: angulus, H.: Tartara, V.: praecordia, O.—As subst n.: se in intimum conicere (balnearum…

intingo.definition: (in-tingō or in-tinguō) —, inctus, ere, to dip, soak.— Only P. perf.: intinctae (faces sanguine), O.

intolerabilis.definition: in-tolerābilis e, adj. with comp, irresistible: vis Romanorum, L.—Insupportable, intolerable: frigus: potentia: regium nomen Romae, L.: vitium, Iu.: multo intolerabilior: Intolerabilius nihil est quam, etc., Iu.

intoleranter.definition: intoleranter adv. with comp. and sup. intolerans, intolerably, immoderately, excessively: dolere: intolerantius insequi, Cs.: intolerantissime gloriarī .

intolerantia.definition: 'intolerantia ae, f intolerans, insufferableness, insolence: superbia atque intolerantia: regis.'

intono.definition: in-tonō uī, ātus, āre, to thunder: Intonat (Iuppiter), O.: pater ter intonuit, V.: intonuit laevum, V.: Eois intonata fluctibus hiemps, fallen in thunder upon, H.—To resound, rattle: clipeum super intonat ingens, V.—F…

intorqueo.definition: in-torqueō torsī, tortus, ēre, to twist, wind about, fold, wrench, distort: paludamento circa bracchium intorto, L.: mentum in dicendo: oculos, V.: intorti capillis angues, entwined, H.: intorti funes, twisted, O.—Fig…

intra2.definition: intrā prep. with acc. 1 intra, within: intra silvas sese continere, Cs.: intra parietes meos: iactum teli, within a javelin's throw, V.: Apenninum, L.: intra oceanum magis, closer to, S.: intra moenia, within the city…

intrabilis.definition: intrābilis e, adj. 2 intro, inaccessible: ōs amnis, L.

intractabilis.definition: in-trāctābilis e, adj., unmanageable, intractable: genus bello, V.: brumae, wild, V.

intractatus.definition: in-trāctātus adj., not managed, untamed, wild: equus, unbroken.— Untried: ne quid intractatum sceleris fuisset, V.

intremo.definition: in-tremō uī —, ere, to tremble, shake within, quake to the centre: intremere murmure Trinacriam, V.: intremuit malus, V.: tellus, O.: genua intremuere, O.: (clamore) intremuere undae, V.

intrepidus.definition: in-trepidus adj., unshaken, undaunted, intrepid: dux, L.: pro se, O.: altaria tangere, Iu.: voltūs, O.: hiemps, i. e. without disturbance, Ta.

introduco.definition: intrō-dūcō dūxī, ductus, ere, to lead in, bring in, introduce, conduct within, admit: Chremem, T.: noctu milites, S.: praesidium, Cs.: suas copias in finīs, Cs.: in cubiculum introductus: ad regem, Cu.: eo navīs, Cs.—…

introductio.definition: intrōductiō ōnis, f introductus, a leading in, introduction: adulescentulorum.

introeo.definition: intro-eō īvī, —, īre, to go in, enter: introire neminem Video, T.: locum hostibus introeundi dare, S.: hostīs, si introire vellent, vocare, Cs.: in domum: in tabernaculum, S.: ad amicam, T.: ad Ciceronem, S.: domum tu…

intromitto.definition: intrō-mittō mīsī, missus, ere, to send in, let in, admit: heri intromissus non est, T.: ut intromissus me trucidaret: legiones (in oppidum), Cs.: sex milia peditum Nolam, L.: ad Senecam alqm, Ta.—With supine acc: Phae…

introrsum.definition: intrōrsum adv. intro+versum, towards the inside, inwards, within: hostem introrsum in media castra accipiunt, L.—Inwardly, within, on the inside: turpis, H.

introrumpo.definition: intrō-rumpō rūpī, ruptus, ere, to break in, enter by force: huc, T.: eā, Cs.

introspicio.definition: intrōspiciō spēxī, spectus, ere intro+specio, to look into, look at: tuam domum: casas omnium.—Fig., to inspect, examine, observe attentively: penitus in omnīs rei p. partes: penitus ceterorum mentī s: fortunam suam, Ta.

intueor.definition: in-tueor itus, ērī, dep., to look upon, look closely at, gaze at: imagines, S.: capite demisso terram, Cs.: solem: ornamenta rei p.: huc atque illuc: ora omnium atque oculos: me, H.: faciem alicuius, N.: nutum illius …

intumesco.definition: in-tumēscō muī, —, ere, inch, to swell up, rise: Amnis . . . inquit ‘Intumui,’ O.—To rise, be elevated: nec intumescit viperis humus, H.—Fig., to swell up, grow louder: quo plenior vox repercussu intumescat, Ta.—To be…

inturbidus.definition: in-turbidus adj., undisturbed: externis rebus annus, Ta.: iuventa, Ta.— Not turbulent: vir, T.

intus.definition: intus adv., on the inside, within: intus est hostis: estne frater intus? T.: Format natura nos intus, H.: in animis: in aede, L.: extra et intus hostem habere, Cs.: clausi (tauri), in the stalls, V.: intus Digna geri,…

intutus.definition: in-tūtus adj., unguarded, unsafe, dangerous: castra Gallorum, L.: intuta moenium, insecure parts, Ta.—Untrustworthy: amicitia, Ta.

inultus.definition: in-ultus adj., without satisfaction, unavenged, unrevenged, not vindicated: perire, S.: Marius ne inultus esset: ne inultos imperatores suos iacere sinerent, L.: numquam moriemur inulti, V.: ne compellarer inultus, H.…

inumbro.definition: in-umbrō āvī, ātus, āre, to overshadow, darken: vestibulum, V.: toros obtentu frondis, V.

inundo.definition: in-undō āvī, ātus, āre, to overflow, inundate: quā fluvius solito magis inundaverat, L.: hanc (terram) inundet aqua: agros, L.: cuius mihi sanguis inundet Guttur, O.: sanguine fossas, V.—Of a throng, to spread, overru…

inurbanus.definition: in-urbānus adj., rustic, ungraceful, unmannerly: habitus orationis.— Of style, inelegant: inurbanum lepido seponere dicto, H.

inuro.definition: in-ūrō ūssī, ūstus, ere, to burn in, burn: notas et nomina gentis, V.: volnere sanguis inustus, O.: inustis barbararum litterarum notis, Cu.—Fig., of persons, to brand, mark: censoriae severitatis notā inuri.—To brand…

inusitatus.definition: in-ūsitātus adj. with comp, unusual, uncommon, extraordinary, very rare: belli ratio: nostris oratoribus lepos: est inusitatum regem reum esse: quid tam inusitatum, quam ut, etc.: species (navium) barbaris inusitatior…

inutilis.definition: in-ūtilis e, adj. with comp, useless, unserviceable, unprofitable: homo: ille, V.: dum meliorem ex ducibus inutilem volnus faceret, L.: ad rem gerendam, Cs.: rei p.: rami, H.: non inutilis ad capiendum consilium tempe…

inutilitas.definition: inūtilitās ātis, f inutilis, hurtfulness, injuriousness: facti.

invado.definition: in-vādō vāsī, vāsus, ere, to go into, enter: ignis, quocumque invasit: urbem, L.: viam, enter upon, V.: tria millia stadiorum, to accomplish, Ta. —To enter violently, move against, rush upon, fall upon, assail, assaul…

invalesco.definition: in-valēscō valuī, —, ere, inch, to become strong, grow powerful: haec defensurus, prout invaluissent, Ta.

invalidus.definition: in-validus adj., not strong, infirm, impotent, weak, feeble: ad munera corporis senectā, L.: volnere, Ta.: senes, V.: quidquid tecum invalidum, V.: corpus, O.—Weak, inadequate, unsuitable: stationes pro castris, L.: i…

invectio.definition: invectiō ōnis, f VAG-, an importing, importation: (rerum) quibus egeremus.—A sailing in, arrival: eodem flumine.

inveho.definition: in-vehō vexī, vectus, ere, to carry in, bring to, introduce: tantum in aerarium pecuniae: quas (opes) mare litoribus invehit, Cu.—Pass, to be carried in, ride into, drive to, be borne in, enter: dictator urbem invehit…

invenio.definition: in-veniō vēnī, ventus, īre, to come upon, find, meet with, light upon: in agro populabundum hostem, L. (navīs) paratas ad navigandum, Cs.: oratores.—Pass: rex Inventus focis, found, V.: Scis, Pamphilam meam inventam c…

inventio.definition: inventiō ōnis, f BA-, the faculty of invention: illa vis quae investigat occulta, etc.—In rhet., invention: excogitatio rerum, etc.

inventor.definition: inventor ōris, m in+BA-, a contriver, author, discoverer, inventor: voluptatum, T.: olei: omnium artium, Cs.: scelerum, V.: legis Volero, proposer, L.: Stoicorum, founder.

inventrix.definition: inventrīx īcis, f inventor, she that finds out, a discoverer: omnium doctrinarum inventrices Athenae: legum: oleae Minerva, V.

invenustus.definition: in-venustus adj., without charm, ungraceful, unattractive: actor: res, Ct.—Without Venus, unfortunate in love: homo, T.

inverecundus.definition: in-verēcundus adj., without shame, unreserved, shameless, immodest: deus, i. e. Bacchus, H.: animi ingenium, Poët. ap. C.

invergo.definition: in-vergō —, —, ere, to incline, pour upon: invergens charchesia mellis, O.: fronti vina, V.

inversio.definition: inversiō ōnis, f VERT-, an inversion: verborum, i. e. irony.

inverto.definition: in-vertō (-vortō) vertī, versus, ere, to turn upside down, turn about, upset, invert, reverse: solum, plough up, V.: Allifanis vinaria, empty, H.: alveos navium invorsos pro tuguriis habere, S.: submovere Euros Pellib…

invesperascit.definition: in-vesperāscit —, ere, impers, it becomes evening, evening is approaching: cum invesperasceret: iam invesperascebat, L.

investigatio.definition: investīgātiō ōnis, f investigo, a searching into, investigation: rerum: veri.

investigator.definition: investīgātor ōris, m investigo, he that searches into, an investigator: rerum: antiquitatis.

investigo.definition: in-vestīgō āvī, ātus, āre, to track, trace out, search after: ad investigandum sagacitas narium. —Fig., to trace out, find out, discover, investigate, search into: neque ille investigatur, Qui est eius pater, T.: cane…

inveterasco.definition: in-veterāscō rāvī, —, ere, inch, to grow old, become fixed, be established, continue long: quibus quisque in locis miles inveteraverit, Cs.: exercitum inveterascere in Galliā moleste ferebant, establish themselves, Cs…

inveteratio.definition: inveterātiō ōnis, f invetero, an inveterate disease, chronic evil.

invetero.definition: inveterō āvī, ātus, āre in+vetus, to make old, give age to: peregrinam novitatem, Cu.— Pass, to grow old, become rooted: unā cum saeclis hominum inveterari: inveteratā gloriā, N.

invicem.definition: in-vicem or in vicem adv., by turns, in turn, one after another, alternately: hi rursus in vicem anno post in armis sunt, Cs.: cum timor atque ira invicem sententias variassent, L.: nos cantabimus invicem, in my turn,…

invictus.definition: in-vīctus adj. with sup, unconquered, unsubdued, unconquerable, invincible: Germani, Cs.: exercitus: gentes, V.: invictus morior, N.: invictissimus civis: res p.: adamas, impenetrable, O.: Medea, inexorable, H.: invic…

invidentia.definition: invidentia ae, f invideo, envy, jealousy.

invideo.definition: in-videō vīdī, vīsus, ēre, to look askance at, cast an evil eye upon: florem liberūm meūm? Att. ap. C.—Fig., to be prejudiced against, be influenced by prejudice: iudex, qui invidet: cui nisi invidisset is, etc.—To en…

invidia.definition: invidia ae, f invidus, envy, grudge, jealousy, ill-will, prejudice: invidiā abducti, Cs.: invidiam sequi, S.: virtus imitatione digna, non invidiā: Sine invidiā laudem invenire, ungrudgingly, T.: invidiā ducum perfidi…

invidiosus.definition: invidiōsus adj. with comp. and sup. invidia, full of envy, invidious: vetustas, O.—Plur m. as subst: omnium invidiosorum animos frangere. — Exciting envy, enviable, envied, causing odium: possessiones: nec caris erat …

invidus.definition: invidus adj. in+VID-, envious, envying: imperator: invida me spatio natura coercuit, O.: populus, N.: aegris, H.: laudis invidus.—As subst, an envious person, hater: Invidus alterius macrescit rebus opimis, H.: istos …

invigilo.definition: in-vigilō āvī, ātus, āre, to watch over, be devoted, be intent: rei p.: malis, O.: Namque aliae victu invigilant, V.: nostris pro casibus, O.

inviolabilis.definition: in-violābilis adj., inviolable: pacis pignus, V.—Invulnerable: alqs, Ta.

invisitatus.definition: in-vīsitātus adj., unseen, unknown: forma: acies, L.: alienigenis, L.—Extraordinary, uncommon, new, strange: supplicia: formae hominum, L.: simulacra, Cu.

inviso.definition: in-vīsō sī, —, ere, to look after, go to see, visit: sacrificium: res rusticas: urbīs, V.: simul haec invisent lumina colles, get sight of, Ct.

invitamentum.definition: invītāmentum ī, n invito, an invitation, allurement, incitement, inducement: invitamenta urbis, attractions: (honos) non invitamentum ad tempus est: ad luxuriam, L.: temeritatis, L.

inerrans.definition: in-errāns tis, adj., not wandering, fixed: stellae.

iniucunditas.definition: iniūcunditās ātis, f iniucundus, unpleasantness: ne quid habeat iniucunditatis oratio.

ingigno.definition: (in-gīgnō) genuī, genitus, ere, to implant, engender: cupiditatem homini: animantibus conservandi sui custodiam.

incurvatus.definition: incurvātus adj. P. of incurvo, bent, crooked, bowed: bacillum: membra dolore, O.

improperatus.definition: improperātus (in-pr-) adj., not hasty, lingering: vestigia, V.

immane.definition: immāne (inm-) adv. immanis, frightfully, fiercely, savagely: leo hians, V.: sonat fluctus, V.

iniucunde.definition: (iniūcundē) adv. iniucundus, unpleasantly. —Only comp: res iniucundius actae.

ignigena.definition: īgnigena ae, m ignis+GEN-, the fire-born, son of fire (of Bacchus), O.

iustificus.definition: iūstificus adj. iustus+2 FAC-, that acts justly: mens deorum, Ct.

inrogatio.definition: inrogātiō (irr-) ōnis, f inrogo, an imposing, adjudicating: multae.

insigniter.definition: īnsīgniter adv. with comp. insignis, remarkably, extraordinarily, notably: amicos diligere: in signius ornari, N.

infideliter.definition: īnfidēliter adv., faithlessly, perfidiously: nec aliquid senatui suadere.

immodeste.definition: immodestē adv. immodestus, immoderately, shamelessly: gloriari, L.

iunctura.definition: iūnctūra ae, f IV-, a joining, uniting, juncture, joint: tignorum, Cs.: iuncturae verticis, sutures, O.: laterum iuncturas fibula mordet, the united ends of the girdle, V.—Fig., a connection: generis, i. e. consanguin…

iuro.definition: iūrō āvī, ātus, āre 2 ius, to swear, take an oath: si aram tenens iuraret: ex animi tui sententiā, without reservation: Boeotum in crasso iurares aëre natum, H.: falsum, swear falsely: vere: testari deos per quos iura…

imberbis.definition: 'imberbis (inb-) e, adj. 2 in+barba, without a beard, beardless: pater: quae Imberbes didicere, H.'

imprudenter.definition: imprūdenter (inpr-) adv. with comp. imprudens, without foresight, ignorantly, inconsiderately: putant: facere, N.: accessit imprudentius, T.

ingrate.definition: ingrātē adv. ingratus, unpleasantly: Sunt quibus ingrate indulgentia servit, O.—Unthankfully, ungratefully: necessitudinis nomen repudiare.

intermenstruus.definition: inter-mēnstruus adj., between months: tempus, the change of moon.

insector.definition: īnsector ātus, arī, dep. freq. insequor, to pursue, follow up: exercitum: herbam rastris, i. e. extirpate, V.—Fig., of speech, to pursue, attack, rail at, inveigh against: ultro Insectere velut melior? lecture, H.: et…

interpretatus.definition: interpretātus adj. P. of interpretor, explained, transtated: nomen: haec ex Graeco carmine, L.

incondite.definition: inconditē adv. inconditus, confusedly, without order: incondite fundit quantum potest.

impigre.definition: impigrē adv. impiger, actively, quickly, readily: hostium res attendere, S.: consulem sequi, L.

imbecille.definition: (imbēcillē) adv. imbecillus, weakly, feebly. —Only comp: imbecillius adsentiri, with hesitation.

iuglans.definition: iūglāns glandis, f Iovis+glans, a walnut, walnut-tree: iuglandium putamina.

imperite.definition: imperītē adv. with comp. and sup. imperitus, unskilfully, ignorantly, awkwardly: facit: quid potuit dici imperitius?: imperitissime dictum.

inrepo.definition: in-rēpō (irr-) rēpsī, —, ere, to creep in, slip in, be stealthily inserted, steal in: eloquentia inrepit in sensūs: in tabulas municipiorum: animos, Ta.

ingenue.definition: ingenuē adv. ingenuus, as becomes his birth, liberally, frankly: educatus: confiteri.

irrisor.definition: inrīsor (irr-) ōris, m RID-, a derider, mocker, scoffer: orationis, C., Pr.

irruptio.definition: inruptiō (irr-) ōnis, f RVP-, a breaking in, invasion, incursion: armatorum in domum: etiamsi inruptio facta nulla sit.

irrequietus.definition: in-requiētus (irr-) adj., unquiet, restless, without repose: Enipeus, O.: Charybdis, O.—Disquieting, causing unrest: sors mea, O.: bella, O.

irreverentia.definition: 'in-reverentia (irr-) ae, f irreverence, disrespect: iuventutis, Ta.: adversus fas nefasque, Ta.'

irrevocatus.definition: in-revocātus (irr-) adj., not called back, without an encore, H.

intuo.definition: intuor —, ī 1 in+tuor, rare for tueor, to gaze upon: qui intuitur nos, T.

inmolo.definition: immolō (in-m-) āvī, ātus, āre, to sprinkle with sacrificial meal; hence, to make a sacrifice, offer, sacrifice, immolate: cum Sulla immolaret: Musis bovem: animalia capta, Cs.: homines, Cs.: cum pluribus dis immolatur…

irritamen.definition: inrītāmen (irr-) inis, n inrito, an incitement, incentive, provocation: opes, animi inritamen avari, O.: sua (tauri) inritamina Poeniceae vestes, O.

irreprehensus.definition: in-reprehēnsus (irr-) adj., blameless, without blame: probitas, O.: responsa, true, O.

illacrimabilis.definition: in-lacrimābilis (ill-) e, adj., unwept, unlamented: omnes inlacrimabiles Urgentur Nocte, H. —Not moved by tears, pitiless: Pluto, H.

irrogatio.definition: inrogātiō (irr-) ōnis, f inrogo, an imposing, adjudicating: multae.

inpremo.definition: imprimō (inpr-) pressī, pressus, ere 1 in+ premo, to press upon, press against: Stamina impresso pollice nentes, O.: Impresso genu nitens, V.: inpressā tellurem reppulit hastā, i. e. raised herself, O.—To stamp, impri…

illacessitus.definition: in-lacessītus (ill-) adj., unprovoked, unattacked: pacem inlacessiti nutrierunt, Ta.: Britanniae pars, undisturbed, Ta.

irretio.definition: inrētiō (irr-) īvī, ītus, īre 1 in+rete, to catch in a net, ensnare, entangle: beluam inretitam tenere.—Fig., to entrap, catch, entangle, ensnare, involve: tacentem te: alquem corruptelarum inlecebris: disputationum l…

intervorto.definition: inter-vertō (-vortō) iī, sus, ere, to turn aside, divert, intercept, embezzle, squander: receptum (consulatum): interversā aedilitate, i. e. passing over: interverso regali hoc dono.

illiberalitas.definition: inlīberālitās (ill-) ātis, f inliberalis, meanness, stinginess: inliberalitatis suspicio.

inmugio.definition: immūgiō (in-m-) iī, —, īre, to bellow in, resound inwardly: immugiit Aetna cavernis, V.: regia luctu, V.

inmigro.definition: immigrō (in-m-) āvī, ātus, āre, to remove, migrate, change abode: in domum.—Fig., of words: immigrasse in suum (locum) diceres, i. e. have found their appropriate use.

illabefactus.definition: 'in-labefactus (ill-) adj., unbroken, uninterrupted: adfinia vincula, O.: concordia, O.'

irremeabilis.definition: in-remeābilis (irr-) e, adj., not to be retraced, from which there is no return: error, V.: unda, i. e. the Styx, V.

inpluo.definition: impluō (in-p-) —, —, ere, to rain upon: summis adspergine silvis, O.

irrumatio.definition: inrumātiō (irr-) ōnis, f beastly obscenity, Ct.

illabor.definition: in-lābor (ill-) lapsus, ī, dep., to flow in, glide in, fall, sink: Si fractus inlabatur orbis, fall to ruins, H.: quo (in stomachum) primo inlabuntur ea, etc.: mediae urbi, V.—Fig., to flow in, penetrate: ad eos (sens…

irrisus.definition: 1) inrīsus P. of inrideo. | 2) inrīsus (irr-) ūs, m RID-, a scoffing, mocking, mockery, derision: inrisui fore, be a laughing-stock, Cs., Ta.: linguam ab inrisu exserens, out of mockery, L.

illaetabilis.definition: in-laetābilis (ill-) e, adj., cheerless, joyless, gloomy, sad: ora, V.: murmur, V.

inmunio.definition: immūniō (inm-) īvī, —, īre, to fortify: praesidium, Ta.

inmordeo.definition: (immordeō or in-m-) —, sus, ēre, to bite into.—Only P. pass.: immorso collo, Pr.: stomachus pernā immorsus, i. e. stimulated, H.

irretortus.definition: 'in-retortus (irr-) adj., not turned back: oculo inretorto, without looking back, H.'

irroro.definition: in-rōrō (irr-) āvī, ātus, āre, to bedew: terras, V.—To moisten, besprinkle, wet: extremo inrorat Aquarius anno, brings rain, V.: caput, O.: crinem aquis, O.: lacrimae misero de corpore Inrorant foliis, O.— To sprinkle…

irresolutus.definition: in-resolūtus (irr-) adj., not loosened: vincula, O.

ilium.definition: 1) Īlium or Īlion ī, n (C., V., H., O.), *)/ilion, or Ilios, ī, f (H., O.), *)/ilios, Ilium, Troy. | 2) (īlium ī, n), see ilia.

Iactus.definition: 1) iactus P. of iacio. | 2) iactus ūs, m IA-, a throwing, casting, hurling, throw, cast: fulminum: Pulveris, V.: teli iactu abesse, a spear's throw, L.: femineus, i. e. by a woman, O.: quatere fenestras Iactibus, i. e. by throwing stones, H.—Of …

iam.definition: 1) iam adj. I. Of time, at the moment, at the present moment, now, at this time, just now, at present: iam satis credis sobrium esse me, T.: saltūs reficit iam roscida luna, V.: Iam melior, iam, diva, precor, V.: iura ip… | 2) iam dūdum, iam iam, iam iamque, iam pridem, iandūdum see iam.

ictus.definition: 1) īctus P. of ico. | 2) īctus ūs, m 1 IC-, a blow, stroke, stab, cut, thrust, bite, sting, wound: uno ictu securis: gladiatoris: scutis uno ictu pilorum transfixis, Cs.: non caecis ictibus volnerari, L.: medicari cuspidis ictum, V.: arboris,…

immutatus.definition: 1) immūtātus (in-m-) adj., unchanged, unaltered. | 2) immūtātus P. of immuto.

impressus.definition: 1) impressus (inpr-) P. of imprimo. | 2) 'impressus (in-pr-) adj., unpressed, not milked: ubera, Pr.'

impulsus.definition: 1) impulsus (inp-) P. of impello. | 2) impulsus (inp-) ūs, m 1 in+1 PAL-, a striking against, push, pressure, shock, impulse: impulsu scutorum copiae pulsae: alieno impulsu moveri: dimotis inpulsu pectoris undis, O.—Fig., incitement, instigation, influence…

imputatus.definition: 1) imputātus (inp-) P. of imputo. | 2) imputātus (inp-) adj. 2 in+putatus, unpruned, untrimmed: vinea, H.

inceptus.definition: 1) inceptus P. of incipio. | 2) (inceptus, ūs) m 1 in+CAP-, a beginning, undertaking (only abl sing.): turpe inceptūst, T.: foedum inceptu, foedum exitu, L.

incestus.definition: 1) incestus adj. 2 in+castus, not religiously pure, unclean, impure, polluted, defiled, sinful, criminal: virum incesto ore lacerare: incesto addidit integrum, punished the good with the bad, H.: an triste bidental Mover… | 2) (incestus, ūs) m 2 in+2 CAD-, unchastity, incest.—Only abl: quaestio de incestu.

incido.definition: 1) incidō cidī, —, ere 1 in+cado, to fall in, fall, light, strike, reach, find the way: umeri surgunt quā tegmina summa, incidit (hasta), V.: Incidit spatium rhombi Implevitque sinūs, i. e. happens into a net, Iu.: in fo… | 2) incīdō cīdī, cīsus, ere 1 in+caedo, to cut into, cut through, cut open, cut away: venas hominis: teneris arboribus incisis, Cs.: pinnas, clip: vites falce, V.: pulmo incisus, divided: linum, sever.—To cut upon, carve,…

incultus.definition: 1) in-cultus adj. with comp, untilled, uncultivated: ager: solum: loca, S.— Plur n. as subst: culta ab incultis notare, L.—Wild, uncultivated: sentes, V.—Neglected, unpeopled, abandoned: via: quid incultius oppidis?—Undr… | 2) in-cultus ūs, m want of cultivation, neglect: incultu foeda eius (loci) facies, S.: honores desertos per incultum, L.

indago.definition: 1) indāgō āvī, ātus, āre indu+1 AG-, to trace out, track: canis natus ad indagandum.— Fig., to investigate, explore, hunt for, trail: quod in causā quaerendum est: indicia exiti: de re p. | 2) indāgō inis, f indu+1 AG-, an encircling with toils, surrounding: saltūs indagine cingunt, V.: indaginis modo silvas persultare, Ta.: velut indagine Samnites agere, hunt like game, L.

indico.definition: 1) indicō āvī, ātus, āre index, to point out, indicate, inform, show, declare, disclose, make known, reveal, betray: de coniuratione, S.: causam pestis, L.: indicatis deprehensisque internuntiis, Cs.: aliquid in volgus, … | 2) in-dīcō dīxī, dictus, ere, to declare publicly, proclaim, publish, announce, appoint: concilium in diem certam, Cs.: forum, V.: ieiunia, H.: dies indicta pugnae, L.: funus ut indicatur, that invitations be issued: div…

indutus.definition: 1) indūtus P. of induo. | 2) (indūtus ūs), m a putting on.—Only dat: quam (vestem) indutui gerebat, Ta.

infra.definition: 1) īnfrā adv. for inferā, sc. parte, on the under side, below, underneath: infra nihil est nisi mortale: partes eae, quae sunt infra quam id quod devoratur: infra Quam solet esse, O.: exemplum infra scriptum est, S.: one… | 2) īnfrā praep. with acc. 1 infra, below, under, beneath: infra oppidum: infra caelum nox cadit, Ta.—Of time, later than: Homerus non infra superiorem Lycurgum fuit.—Of size, smaller than: magnitudine paulo infra elephan…

ingressus.definition: 1) ingressus P. of ingredior. | 2) ingressus ūs, m 1 in+GRAD-, an advancing, walking, gait: ingressus, cursus, accubitio: prohiberi ingressu, could not stir, Cs.: instabilis, L.— Fig.: ingressūs capere, begins, V.—A going in, entering: in forum: ingres…

iniectus.definition: 1) iniectus P. of inicio. | 2) (iniectus) ūs, m inicio, a casting on, throwing over.—Only abl: multae vestis, Ta.

iniussus.definition: 1) in-iūssus adj., unbidden, voluntary, of one's own accord: cantare Iniussi numquam desistant, H.: iniussae veniunt ad mulctra capellae, H.: iniussa virescunt Gramina, spontaneous, V.—Plur n. as subst: Non iniussa cano,… | 2) (in-iūssus, ūs) m without command.—Only abl: iniussu suo et civitatis, Cs.: iniussu praetoris: signa referunt, without orders, L.

insero.definition: 1) īn-serō sēvī, situs, ere, to implant, ingraft: piros, V.: fissā modo cortice virgam Inserit, O.: ramos, H.: videmus insita mā la Ferre pirum, V.— Fig., to implant, ingraft, fix: num qua tibi vitiorum inseverit olim Na… | 2) īn-serō seruī, sertus, ere, to put in, introduce, insert, thrust: caput in lecticam: insertae fenestrae, V.: trecentos (in navem), H.: oculos in pectora, O.: caput in tentoria, L.: falces insertae longuriis, Cs.: subt…

insomnium.definition: 1) īnsomnium ī, n 1 in+somnus, a dream. —Sing., Ta.— Plur., T., V., Tb. | 2) īnsomnium ī, n 2 in+somnus, sleeplessness.—Only plur: insomnia portare ocellis, Pr.

intellectus.definition: 1) intellēctus P. of intellego. | 2) intellēctus ūs, m 1 LEG-, a perception, discernment: hiems et ver intellectum ac vocabula habent, i. e. are recognized, Ta.

intro.definition: 1) intrō adv. * interus; ANA-, to the inside, within, in: intro ad nos venit, T.: intro est itum, Cs.: vocari: vocata centuria, L. | 2) intrō āvi, ātus, āre * interus; ANA-, to go into, enter: limen: olearum ordinem: domum, N.: portas, L.: id (flumen), S.: fluminis ripas, to come between, V.: ut domus est intrata, O.: ante quam (animus) in corpus intr…

istic.definition: 1) istic aec, oc and uc (with -ne, istucine), pron demonstr. iste+ce.— Referring to that which is at hand or related to the person addressed, that of yours, that mentioned by you: istaec res, T.: circum istaec loca commo… | 2) istīc adv., there, in that place, where you are: quid istic tibi negotist? T.: quoniam istic sedes: quocumque istic loco constitisti, L.—Herein, in this affair, on this occasion: Neque istic, neque alibi, T.: Istic su…

iugis.definition: 1) iūgis e, adj. IV-, joined together: auspicium, i. e. of a yoke of oxen. | 2) iūgis e, adj. VIV-, fresh, living, perennial: putei: aqua, S., H.

iussus.definition: 1) iūssus P. of iubeo. | 2) (iūssus, ūs) m an order, command, decree, ordinance (only abl sing.): vestro iussu coactus: lecti iussu populi, L.: sine populi iussu, S.: dei, V.: Neronis, Iu.

iuxta.definition: 1) iūxtā adv. for * iūgistā, abl f. sup. from iūgis, near to, nigh, near at hand, near, near by, hard by, close to, by the side of: legio, quae iuxta constiterat, Cs.: sellam iuxta ponere, S.: furiarum maxima iuxta Accub… | 2) iūxtā praep. with acc. 1 iuxta, very near, close to, near to, hard by: iuxta eum castra posuit, Cs.: iuxta focum agunt, Ta.: hanc (aram) iuxta, N.: vicina Ceraunia iuxta, V.—Next to, immediately after, beside, on a pa…

imbecillis.definition: imbēcillis, -e (= imbēcillus, -a, -um): debole, fiacco, senza forze

infer.definition: infer (= inferus), -a, -um: che sta sotto, infero; pl. inferī: gli dèi di sotto, i morti

inopinor.definition: inopīnor, -ārī: non aspettarsi — di norma nel ptc. inopinans: che non s'aspetta, ignaro
